description: BREDEM, the Building Research Establishment Domestic Energy Model, is a calculation method that estimates a dwelling's energy consumption from its characteristics. The BREDEM 2012 technical description by Henderson and Hart, version 1.1 of July 2013 with corrections of January 2015, is a free 37-page PDF. It is a monthly method that, like SAP, follows BS EN ISO 13790, and works through ten steps: lights, appliances and cooking; water heating; specific heat loss; thermal mass; solar and internal gains; mean internal temperature; space heating; cooling; and electricity from photovoltaics and wind turbines. Outputs are fuel requirements by end use that convert to costs or CO2 with suitable factors. Coverage: UK dwellings. Access: free specification download; implementations are up to the user. Licence: BRE copyright. Caveats: a monthly method, so it gives no hourly or peak results. Simulation uses: housing stock energy models and retrofit benefit estimates, as the specification itself suggests. Related records: the Cambridge Housing Model and the CREST Demand Model.
